newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Santos sees big gas future in Queensland.
newsitem.headline: Santos sees big gas future in Queensland.

text.p: Oil and gas producer Santos Ltd said on Thursday that south-west Queensland's Cooper-Eromanga Basin contained some potentially large gas developments which if successful would substantially add to the group's reserves.

"One field structure alone has the potential to hold one trillion cubic feet of gas in tight reservoirs," Santos general manager for finance, Graeme Bethune, said in remarks prepared for an oil and gas conference here.
"A major project to evaluate this field is underway," Bethune told the conference, sponsored by stock brokers Wilson HTM.
Bethune said Santos expected Queensland's Cooper Basin to contribute about 25 percent of total group production in a few years compared with about 15 percent currently.
Santos was also in a good position to supply gas to eastern and southern Australia from other areas, he said.
Linkage between the Amadeus-Darwin pipeline and the Ballera-Mt Isa pipeline only required a new 580 km link, he said.

"Completion of this new link and the connection of offshore Northern Territory gas fields to Darwin would make this gas available into Queensland and to South Australia and New South Wales," Bethune said.
He said potential large industrial customers in the Northern Territory, in particular the Gove Alumina refinery, would help achieve economies of scale to make such a project viable.
The Mereenie oil and gas field in the Amadeus Basin, in which Santos holds interests, was yet to be fully appraised, he added.

Santos' interests in the Minerva gas field in offshore Victoria, the onshore Otway Basin and the Yolla field in Bass Strait were also likely to play a role in supplying gas to southern states, Bethune said.
He said a planned gas pipeline from Papua New Guinea to Townsville, northern Queensland, had been exciting interest but would require major customers in Townsville.

"So far as the bulk of Queensland demand for gas in central southern and western Queensland is concerned, the Cooper Basin is well located to continue to be the most competitive source of supply," Bethune said.
Santos announced on Wednesday that its Thoar-2 gas appraisal well in south-west Queensland had proved successful, flowing gass at a rate of 7.3 million cubic feet per day.
Thoar 2 is 1.9 km south-east of Thoar 1 and about 70 km south of the Ballera Gas Centre.
Santos is the operator and has a 58.8625 percent interest.

Other participants are Exxon Corp unit Delhi Petroleum with 23.2 percent, Boral Ltd's Boral Energy Resources Ltd with 16.5 percent, Australian Hydrocarbons Ltd with 1.2 percent and Oil Co of Australia Ltd with 0.2375 percent.
